precepts.text: Precept brought by the captain on justifying yourself: if I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me. The margin renders justify as cleanse or clear self. Deceiving yourself is telling yourself, I am already cleansed, I am already clear, while refusing the reproof and instruction the teachers bring. Video played in class: sometimes you have to let people suffer the consequences of choices they made knowingly, because rescue delays the learning; growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. As David said, it is good that I was afflicted. Teachers cannot carry everybody; and teachers, do not weaponize the scriptures either: do not be the brother that is wise and teacheth many, and is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to an accountability you will not hold yourself to.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
Saul is in denial: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me”. Samuel breaks down the rebuke, and Saul tells the prophet he is wrong.

Then he lays the spoil on the people again: “the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed”.

note.label: Job 9: No Man Can Contend With God

precepts.why:
“Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.” Job cannot see him, but he is there: “The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.”

There is nothing we can do to escape him; his omnipresence and omnipotence reach wherever we go. We can run but we cannot hide. And when he taketh away, who can hinder him? No man can say to God, Lord what are you doing, I do not agree, I veto that, I object your honor. If he will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers stoop under him, so how much less can Job choose out his words to reason with him. Though he were righteous, he would not answer, but make supplication to his judge.

note.label: Job 9: No Man Can Contend With God

precepts.why:
“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”. Job is pleading his case, saying he cannot speak against God, but this one thing he does see: the earth is handed to the wicked. Who are the wicked according to the Bible? It is Edom, Esau. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

This is prophetic. During Job's time Esau was in the clefts of the rocks, the cave peoples, and he was not rich, but the wicked always prosper. Now they prosper with the buildings, the Maseratis, the new Hummers, while the righteous of the Most High are steady being afflicted, getting a little mercy, coming through, staying strong. They shall build, but the Most High will throw down, and they are called the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation for ever.

The Most High destroyeth both the perfect and the wicked, for every man has his time under the sun; the righteous perish off the earth and the wicked perish off the earth, but we have different judgments at the end. And he covereth the faces of the judges thereof: the judges are the Israelites, the saints, for we have a book of Judges. People say only God can judge me, but that will not fly, because those who know his laws and keep his statutes and commandments are able to judge the small matters between brother and brother, sister and sister, neighbors, and situations in the church.
